chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: Recording piano with his kids, Two Honeys in a Comb
summary: He recorded with his young trio, whose trumpeter Lucius scatted and played harmonized lines, until the Army took him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: You made some recordings on piano, didn't you? In the '50s or something like that?

Yes, I made a recording with Meyer -- with my kids. Yeah. Called them Two Honeys in a Comb. Oh, those kids were something else. Those kids were something else. I'll show you their pictures. Or did I show you this the other day?
I don't think you did. Oh, yeah.
They're kind of dusty now, getting dust on here. Now, what this --

Yeah, this is Lucius? Now, what Lucius would do with the trumpet, where I would write for them, when they would take an outcourse, like, they would be singing, and when they'd do the outcourse, then -- like Ella Fitzgerald sang sometimes, she goes (scatting), --
He would do the (scatting), they would do the second to that, the second and third parts to that.
Oh, they were something else. (Scatting). That's the way he was going.

And he'd be punching, (unintelligible). They would tag, and he'd be right in there. Now, you know I really hated to see that outfit break up. But when the Army took him, and he came back, and that was it.
